coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: The Canyon
record.summary: The first Mission Rock residential building: a 23-story, 283-unit rental tower by MVRDV on Parcel A at 3rd Street, with two office floors and ground-floor retail; TCO May 2023, first residents June 1, 2023, opening ceremony June 21, 2023. It also houses the district energy plant that serves the whole neighborhood.

facts.value: Mission Rock Partners (San Francisco Giants and Tishman Speyer); vertical owner Mission Rock Parcel A Owner, L.L.C.
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 337); 75-year prepaid parcel lease

102 BMR units (36%) at 90%, 120% and 150% AMI as built and leased from 2023 (10 / 54 / 38); the Port Commission approved a reduction to 73 (19 at 90% AMI, 54 at 120% AMI, none at 150%) on March 11, 2025 (Resolution 25-17), with the next step being Board of Supervisors approval of the Housing Plan amendment; no later source read gives the outcome of that step
240 ft (73 m) per MVRDV and the Design Controls' Block A maximum; SF YIMBY reports 258 ft
375,000 to 376,000 (221,140 residential, 49,290 office, 14,950 to 15,950 retail, 4,180 amenity) per SF YIMBY; 34,900 m2 per MVRDV
residential over two office floors and ground-floor retail; 5-story plinth with tower
Houses the district energy system (heating and cooling) that serves all of Mission Rock

An office lease in Parcel A was signed by October 2023 (Port); Capgemini had officially moved in by April 26, 2024 (SF YIMBY: 'has officially moved into their offices in the base of the Canyon'; DataSF lists its business location start as 2024-04-01)
75 years, fully prepaid at execution (Lease No. L-16703, October 6, 2020)
Port receives 1.5% of net refinancing and net sale proceeds under the parcel lease; definitions amended by Port Resolution 23-46 and Board file 231116 (final action December 8, 2023)
201910073782 (site permit, new construction; filed October 7, 2019, approved October 26, 2020)

open_questions: Construction cost of The Canyon: no source found; the Port memos cover only the horizontal (site-level) budget.
Street address: DataSF's Assessor roll gives 1011 3rd St for lot 8719B002 and Wikipedia gives 1023 3rd St; DBI permits use 1023 3rd St. No Port document read gives the address.
Whether the Board of Supervisors approved the March 2025 Housing Plan amendment (30% to 20% per phase) and the Parcel A lease amendment: not found on Legistar during this pass.
Groundbreaking date: Wikipedia says December 2020 without a citation; Swinerton says early 2021; no Port document dates it. Kept as approximate 2021.
Height: MVRDV says 240 ft, SF YIMBY 258 ft. A building permit or the Planning design-review record (CPC 2013.0208PHA-02) would settle it.
status.csv and milestones.csv previously dated the opening ceremony June 24, 2024; the sources say June 21, 2023 (SF YIMBY, MVRDV); corrected 2026-09-29.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (until 2020 the parcel was the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.
Whether Quik Dog opened in November 2025 (Hoodline preview) or January 2026 (SF Standard, July 2026: 'opened in January'): the sources read disagree, so its opening date is left blank.

record.notes: The Canyon -- Mission Rock Parcel A ('Building A, i.e., The Canyon', SF YIMBY 2022; the Port's Oct 2023 memo names 'Parcel A, "The Canyon"'), 283-unit MVRDV-designed residential tower at 1011-1023 3rd St (DataSF Assessor address 1011 3rd St; Wikipedia gives 1023 3rd St); completed in 2023 (Port temporary certificate of occupancy May 2023; MVRDV: 'The Canyon on San Francisco's waterfront is complete'), officially opened in a ceremony on June 21, 2023 (MVRDV; Wikipedia's infobox says June 23)
